labels.notes: No ``**`label`**`` mark appears anywhere in the file (it says 'no label is marked', :9-10), and the REPORT has labels: []. Faithfulness was read against the target's evidence and against sbierski2023c.txt:328-358, :704-739 and :1057-1145. (1) The six fields of PastBoundaryChartData (:113-142) are the evidence's (i)-(vi) verbatim: p ∈ Ũ, p ∉ W; V ≤ W ⊓ Ũ; ∀ x ∈ V, I⁺(x,Ũ) ⊆ I⁺(x,V); C.ChronalCurveOn Ũ γ̃ 0 1 with γ̃ 0 = p and γ̃ (0,1] ⊆ V; s₀ ∈ (0,1) with closure(I⁺(p,Ũ) ∩ I⁻(γ̃ s₀,Ũ)) compact and ⊆ Ũ; ∀ compact K ⊆ Ũ ∃ σ chronal in Ũ over [0,1] with σ 0 ∉ W, σ (0,1] ⊆ V ∖ K and γ̃ 1 ≪_Ũ σ 1. Nothing is weakened. (2) Every field follows from Sbierski's past boundary chart (Prop 2.1 time-reversed, with (4.1) and the choice of s₀ at :1077). (i): p̃ lies on ∂ι(M), so p̃ ∉ ι(M). (ii): V = Ũ_>. (iii): (2.4) reversed, since a future timelike curve of Ũ from Ũ_> stays in Ũ_>. (iv): s ↦ (s,0), reparametrised. (v): the I-diamond lies in the compact J_{g̃_w}-diamond. (vi): x₀ is taken off the compact projection of K into the open cube, and the vertical line from (f(x₀),x₀) runs up to the slab of (4.1). So the predicate is no stronger than Sbierski's chart, and ¬PastBoundaryChart implies there is no Sbierski chart: Lean ≥ the paper's abstract step. (3) The hypotheses of the main theorem (:305-311) are exactly the evidence's: T2, second countable, CausallyArcConnectedOn W, FutureOneConnectedOn W, hcaus in the shape of PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy.lean:469, and (A) and (B) as written in the evidence. Each is implied by Sbierski's setting: I⁺ is realised by timelike curves; GH gives causal; Prop 3.1 gives future one-connectedness for d ≥ 2; Prop 3.6 gives (A), since in FLRW every past-inextensible timelike curve has t → 0, and gives (B) at every point, by no particle horizons. These are hypotheses, i.e. layer 3, and the checklist says so. (4) The future form (:345), the (4.2)/(4.3) lemmas and the extension corollary (:513) are correctly stated time reversals and transports. The corollary takes the ladder nodes on N and names OQ-154 (:509-512). (5) Thm 1.5 itself, for FLRW, is not claimed: Prop 2.1 (boundary point ⇒ chart), Prop 3.1 and Prop 3.6 are layer 3. The checklist row 'conclusion: ∂⁻ι(M) = ∅ ✓' overstates this; see the findings.

The hypotheses are ladder properties at W (CausallyArcConnectedOn, FutureOneConnectedOn, antisymmetry inline) plus the declared (A) and (B). The extension corollary takes the nodes CausallyArcConnected, FutureOneConnected and IsCausal on N.

Vacuity (a). The target's evidence, deliverable (v), asks for a joint witness of the theorem's hypotheses: W = Ioi 0 on the timelike line. It is delivered (timelikeLine_flrwType_hypotheses_posHalfLine, :603). The evidence assigns an instance of the predicate explicitly to layer 3 ('That the predicate has an instance is layer 3: T-loc-minkowski-past-boundary-chart'). That target exists in programme/roadmap.toml (planned, depends on T-abs-flrw-type), and its title is 'So T-abs-flrw-type's predicate is not vacuous'. The gap is therefore within the target's acceptance and disclosed (:45-47, :67; REPORT findings and what_remains). It is not major. The docstring could state it more plainly (minor finding 1).

Vacuity (b). I looked for a structural contradiction among the fields under the ETT axioms of Causality.lean (relations of opens, monotone, I± open) and found none. A 1+1 Minkowski sketch with the library's staticCausality: M = ℝ×ℝ, W = {t > 0}, p = 0, Ũ = (-1,1)×(-1/4,1/4), V = W ⊓ Ũ, γ̃(s) = (s/2, 0). (i) holds. (ii) holds. (iii): a Lipschitz<1 graph of Ũ starting at time t(x) > 0 stays in V, so staticLt Ũ x y implies staticLt V x y. (iv): the vertical segment is 0-Lipschitz, hence chronal in every open N around each of its points. (v): for any s₀ ∈ (0,1), the closed diamond from 0 to (s₀/2,0) has |x| ≤ s₀/4 < 1/4 and t ≤ s₀/2 < 1, so it is compact and lies in Ũ. (vi): for compact K ⊆ Ũ, take x₀ ∈ (-1/4,1/4) off the compact projection of K and σ(τ) = (0.9τ, x₀). Then σ 0 has t = 0, so σ 0 ∉ W; σ (0,1] lies in V ∖ K; and (1/2,0) ≪_Ũ (0.9,x₀) by the straight segment, of slope < 0.625. So the predicate is plausibly inhabited in dimension 2. That matches T-loc-minkowski-past-boundary-chart's planned instance (Ũ = (−1,1)×B(0,1/10)), and there (A) fails, as the evidence says. Galilean 'absolute time' causalities cannot carry an instance: K = the closure of the (v) diamond contains every time slice of Ũ between p and γ̃ s₀, so σ cannot cross it. That agrees with the closer's remark. timelikeLine_not_pastBoundaryChart (:534) is a genuine one-dimensional obstruction (an intermediate-value argument), not a sign of global unsatisfiability.

findings.what: Nowhere does the file say plainly that the predicate's satisfiability is not shown in Lean. The disclosure is in 'What is proved' item 5 (:45-47: 'these witnesses show the hypotheses consistent, not the predicate inhabited'). SCOPE says only 'an instance is `T-loc-minkowski-past-boundary-chart`' (:67), which reads as if the instance existed. The main theorem's docstring is silent. If PastBoundaryChart had no inhabitant, the theorem would be empty. Its non-vacuity rests today on an informal Minkowski 1+1 check (sketched in this audit's checks), which a planned layer-3 target has yet to formalise.
findings.fix: Add a SCOPE bullet, for example: 'No instance of PastBoundaryChart is constructed in this file, and none exists on the timelike line (timelikeLine_not_pastBoundaryChart). The main theorem is non-vacuous once T-loc-minkowski-past-boundary-chart (planned, layer 3) proves the Minkowski half-space instance.' Repeat its first clause in the docstring of not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType. The ladder keeper should leave the proposed boundary-chart node and consequence unrecorded until that instance lands.

findings.what: The checklist row 'conclusion: ∂⁻ι(M) = ∅ | ✓ ¬ C.PastBoundaryChart W Ũ p' overstates the result. The Lean concludes that there is no ETT past boundary chart. Sbierski's ∂⁻ι(M) = ∅ follows only through Prop 2.1 (every past boundary point has a chart), which is layer 3 (T-loc-c0-past-boundary-chart). Likewise, the rows for Prop 3.6 (:58-59) and for the chart (:60) are marked ✓, although Prop 3.6 enters as hypotheses (A) and (B) and the chart as a programme definition. Thm 1.5 for FLRW K = +1 is not proved here: Prop 2.1, Prop 3.1 (future one-connectedness) and Prop 3.6 for FLRW are all layer 3, and SCOPE does not list them as not proved. The corollary's docstring ends 'Sbierski's ∂⁻ι(M) = ∅, abstractly' (:512).
findings.fix: Mark the conclusion row '⚠ reading: no ETT past boundary chart. ∂⁻ι(M) = ∅ needs Prop 2.1 (T-loc-c0-past-boundary-chart)'. Mark the Prop 3.6 rows '⚠ assumed (hypotheses (A), (B))'. Add a SCOPE bullet: 'Thm 1.5 itself (FLRW, K = +1, d ≥ 2) is not proved here. Prop 2.1, Prop 3.1 and Prop 3.6 for FLRW are layer 3, and enter as the chart definition and as hypotheses.'

notes: No major finding. The main theorem is a faithful Lean ≥ form of Thm 1.5's abstract step (§4.1). Every field of the predicate is derivable from Sbierski's chart, so 'no ETT chart' implies 'no Sbierski chart'. The predicate is plausibly inhabited in Minkowski 1+1, so the theorem is not vacuous in principle, but this remains to be formalised by T-loc-minkowski-past-boundary-chart.
